1.

Supplementary rejoinder affidavit on behalf of the applicant and supplementary counter affidavit
on behalf of the informant, filed in Court today, are taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 38/2024 under Section 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Indirapuram, District Ghaziabad with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
Applicant is husband of deceased.
The marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place on 18.02.2017 and out of that marriage, they have a three years old daughter.
Before incident for a period of six years, there had been no complaint regarding any dowry demand or harassment of deceased.
The allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased levelled against the applicant are wholly false.
It was submitted that deceased has committed suicide and after applicant came to know about the incident, she was taken to the hospital.
The informant and his family members were present at the time of inquest proceedings on 09.01.2024.
In postmortem report, except ligature mark, no other injury has been shown on the body of deceased and that cause of death has been shown as ante-mortem hanging.
It was further submitted that on several occasions applicant has transferred money to the informant and thus, there was absolutely no question of demand of any dowry.

In this connection, it was submitted that applicant has transferred Rs. 50,000/- on 28.12.2017, Rs. 1,00,000/- on 24.05.2019, Rs. 60,000/- on 25.05.2019,
Rs. 49,000/- on 29.08.2019, Rs. 49,000/- on 23.12.2019 and Rs. 1,00,000/- on 24.12.2019 to the informant and the same is supported by documentary evidence, which has been annexed as annexure no 6 to the bail application.
Further, applicant has given Rs. 3 lacs in cash to the informant on the occasion of marriage of sister of deceased and at the time of admission of brother of deceased in B.Tech course.
Applicant has subscribed a policy of Rs. 2 crore in which deceased was shown nominee.

Applicant has purchased a flat at Shipra Rivera Gyan Khand-III, Indirapuram,
Ghaziabad which was purchased in the name of applicant as well as his wife Shikha (deceased).

Elder brother of applicant was working in New Zealand and applicant has applied for visa for himself, his wife (deceased) and child, which further goes to show that there had been good relations between applicant and deceased.
The minor child of deceased is being maintained and looked-after by the mother of applicant.

5. Learned counsel has further submitted that on 09.01.2024 there was death anniversary of the father of applicant and only some hot talk has taken place due to minor issue and the deceased went into her room and committed suicide.

Learned counsel has referred record of whatsapp chat between applicant and informant, which clearly indicates that on several occasions applicant has financially helped the informant and there were cordial relations between them.
The demand of dowry is not reflected in any of the chat record.
Copies of various transactions of money were also referred to show that applicant had been continuously providing financial help to the informant and his family.
It was submitted that in view of these facts and circumstances, there was absolutely no occasion on the part of applicant to make demand of dowry or to harass the deceased.

Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 10.01.2024, having no criminal history, and in case applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6.
Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of deceased.
There are allegations that deceased was being harassed on account of dowry.
Applicant has failed to satisfy that if the deceased was not being harassed for dowry, why she has committed suicide.
After the incident, applicant did not inform the informant and it was his elder brother, who has informed the informant about the incident.
It was submitted that deceased was an educated lady having MBA degree and earlier she was gainfully employed.
Applicant has been charge-sheeted on the basis of evidence.

It was submitted that in view Pradeep Singh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53228952/

sentences.text: of the aforesaid facts and allegations, applicant is not entitled for bail.
7. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

8. It is apparent from the record that applicant is husband of deceased and their marriage has taken place about six years prior to the incident and out of that marriage, they have a three years old daughter.
It appears from the record of transactions of bank account that on several occasions applicant has transferred various amount to the informant.

In postmortem report, except ligature mark, no other injury has been shown on the body of deceased and cause of death has been shown as ante-mortem hanging.
9.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, material on record, including the record of financial transactions shown between applicant and informant, whatsapp chat record and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

10. Let the applicant Pradeep Singh Yadav involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii.
The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.
